concepts.label: Infant photograph eyes requirement
concepts.definition: Standard permitting an infant's eyes to be partially or completely closed in passport photographs.
concepts.quote: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

scope_quotes: Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:
scope_text: Applies to photographs of infants, where the goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained.
choice_text: The infant's eyes may be either partially closed or completely closed.
object_quote: the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's
object: the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's
summary: In infant photographs, it is acceptable if the infant's eyes (particularly a newborn's) are partially or completely closed.
quote: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

concepts.label: Infant head support
concepts.definition: Permission to discreetly support an infant's head in a passport photograph.
concepts.quote: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

scope_quotes: Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:
summary: An infant's head may be discreetly supported in a photograph, for example using a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.
quote: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

concepts.label: Infant head tilt
concepts.definition: Permission allowing an infant's head to be tilted in photographs.
concepts.quote: Head tilt is acceptable for infants;

summary: Head tilt is acceptable in photographs for infants.
quote: Head tilt is acceptable for infants;

concepts.label: Prohibition of parent face in infant photo
concepts.definition: Rule prohibiting a parent's face from appearing in an infant's photograph.
concepts.quote: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

scope_quotes: in the photograph of the infant.
scope_text: In the photograph of an infant.
summary: A parent's face must not be in the photograph of the infant.
quote: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

concepts.label: Requesting new photograph
concepts.definition: Requirement to request a replacement photograph when the submitted photograph fails to meet specified standards.
concepts.quote: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:

scope_quotes: if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:
scope_text: If the photograph submitted does not meet the specified requirements.
logic_text: if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements
summary: You must request a new photograph if the submitted photograph does not meet the requirements.
quote: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:

concepts.label: Photograph color requirement
concepts.definition: Requirement that submitted photographs be in color.
concepts.quote: The photograph must be in color;

context_quotes: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:
summary: The photograph must be in color.
quote: The photograph must be in color;

concepts.label: Photograph recency and likeness
concepts.definition: Standards concerning when the photo should be taken and that it must represent a good likeness and satisfactorily identify the applicant.
concepts.quote: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

typed_values.name: photo recency limit
typed_values.quote: within six months of submitting the application

logic_text: within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application
action_quote: be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify
action: be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of, and satisfactorily identify
summary: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of the applicant, and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of application.
quote: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

concepts.label: Change in hairstyle or facial hair
concepts.definition: Acceptability standard for photo differences in hairstyle or facial hair compared to submitted ID.
concepts.quote: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

scope_quotes: if it still is a good likeness of the applicant
scope_text: If the photograph still is a good likeness of the applicant.
choice_quote: change in hairstyle or facial hair
choice_text: A change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted.
logic_text: change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant
object_quote: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted
object: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted
summary: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair compared to the submitted identification document is acceptable provided it remains a good likeness of the applicant.
quote: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

concepts.label: Re-use of citizenship or naturalization certificate photograph
concepts.definition: Descriptive possibility that applicants might seek to re-use photos appearing on citizenship or naturalization certificates.
concepts.quote: Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization.

choice_quote: submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization
choice_text: Either a submitted U.S. Certificate of Citizenship or a Certificate of Naturalization.
logic_text: submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization
object_quote: a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization
object: a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization
summary: Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph shown on their submitted U.S. Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization.
quote: Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization.

concepts.label: Certificate photo age possibility
concepts.definition: Observation that certificate issuance dates do not guarantee that the depicted photograph was taken within six months of application submission.
concepts.quote: even if the certificate itself was recently issued, because of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services processing times, the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.

typed_values.name: photo recency window
typed_values.quote: within six months of submitting the application

scope_quotes: even if the certificate itself was recently issued
scope_text: Even if the certificate itself was recently issued.
context_quotes: Be aware that even if the certificate itself was recently issued, because of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services processing times, the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.

summary: Even if a citizenship or naturalization certificate was recently issued, processing times at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services mean the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.
